Subject: Data access controls & support access - post-demo follow-up

Hi Anna -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for taking the time to walk through FinTrust's use case. As promised, a short recap and our proposed next steps focused on the data handling / access control items you raised: 

1) PII classification & handling
- Redwood supports token-level and record-level redaction workflows. We can configure automatic PII masking for fields you mark as sensitive in the ingestion pipeline.

2) Data residency & retention
- Hosted option: region-specific tenancy is available (we can pin FinTrust to us-west for production).
- Retention: configurable per-customer retention windows; defaults are 30/90/365 days with longer archival options.

3) Access controls (RBAC, least privilege)
- RBAC support with role templates (viewer, analyst, admin, support-readonly).
- Break-glass process: time-limited elevated sessions with audit logging + automated notifications.

4) Support access & logging
- Support engineers only get scoped, time-bound access; all actions audited and available in the audit log export (S3 / API).

Attached: redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf (SOC2 + controls overview), rbac-diagram.png, and a draft mutual-action-plan.xlsx for next steps.

Next steps:
- Rishi to answer the technical RBAC/break-glass questions below (by EOD).
- Can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your security/IT team next week? I'm proposing Tue 8/18 or Wed 8/19 morning PT.

Thanks again - looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec and IT teams: 

- PII: When Redwood says "automatic PII masking", can you confirm whether the raw PII is ever persisted in plaintext on disk or in memory on hosted deployments? We need to know what is logged and whether we can enforce field-level encryption.

- Support access: For the break-glass flow, what triggers an access request? Is there an approval workflow tied to our SSO (SAML/Okta)? What is the max session duration and how are sessions revoked?

- Audit/logging: We need immutable audit logs for all administrative actions and support sessions. Can logs be forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk) in near real-time?

- Data residency: We have a policy that production PII must remain in-region (US). Are there cross-region backups or metadata replication that could leak residency?

We'd like written answers for our procurement pack and to get these into our security questionnaire. Can Rishi join a short call to answer technical questions?

Thanks,
Anna Li
Head of Security Programs, FinTrust
anna.li@fintrust.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data access controls & support access - post-demo follow-up

Hi team - answering Anna's questions below; copying Anna so she has the technical notes in thread. Short answers first, followed by a few implementation details.

1) PII persistence/encryption
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): We never persist plaintext PII in our long-term storage for customers who opt-in to PII masking. In the ingestion pipeline we support field-level tokenization and envelope encryption. Raw plaintext may exist transiently in memory during processing but is not written to persistent disk in plaintext.
- All customer data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if you choose the private-key option.

2) Support access / break-glass
- Break-glass is triggered by customer-initiated request (via Console or Support portal) or by an automated alert if you grant emergency escalation rights. Approval workflow can integrate with SSO via SAML/OAuth to enforce approvers from your org (we support Okta/OneLogin).
- Max session duration configurable; default is 2 hours for break-glass. Sessions are time-limited, require justification, and are recorded. Revocation is immediate via the control plane and any active sessions are terminated.

3) Audit/logging and SIEM integration
- All admin/support actions are logged with user, timestamp, affected resources, and session transcript refs. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk) via syslog/HTTPS in near-real-time or exported to an S3 bucket with object immutability options.

4) Data residency and replication
- Production tenant objects (storage and backups) can be pinned to a single region. Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default for tenants that require strict residency. Metadata used for global routing (minimal operational metadata) is pseudonymized; we can provide a data flow diagram in the security packet.

Attachments: rbac-diagram.png (illustrates role templates and scoped support roles). I also attached a short tech note we can include in the questionnaire if helpful.

Open question for Marissa: I recommend offering FinTrust the customer-managed KMS key option and disabling cross-region replication. Also propose the break-glass approval integrate with their existing Okta group to avoid ad-hoc approvals.

Happy to join a call - I'm available Tue 8/18 9:30-11:30 PT or Wed 8/19 10:00-12:00 PT.
